K1.stone_why: A condensed, slightly angular slab-like serif that feels sturdy and grounded but more like a book face than cut stone.
K1.carving_why: The heavy S, O and set numbers show some flat, angled cuts on curves, but the effect is mild and mostly reads as ink.
K1.calm_why: The narrow, dark bold and tightly packed capitals make it a little dense and insistent rather than quiet.
K1.personality_why: The condensed, chunky, slightly rustic forms are distinctive and memorable.
K1.inscription_why: The capitals are narrow and compressed, far from the broad, square proportions of Roman inscriptional caps.
K1.oblique_why: A true italic with a consistent slant and clear contrast with the upright, though it reads a bit cramped at 13 px.
K1.small_why: The 13 px lines are sharp and legible, but the narrow letters and tight spacing make them slightly dense.

K2.stone_why: A neutral grotesque sans that reads as screen UI, with nothing lapidary about it.
K2.carving_why: The display sizes have smooth, mechanical curves with no facets or chiselled terminals.
K2.calm_why: The rhythm is even and orderly, though the bold numbers have a slightly technical, assertive feel.
K2.personality_why: A generic corporate sans that could belong to any app.
K2.inscription_why: Monoline grotesque capitals bear no relation to Roman inscriptional capitals.
K2.oblique_why: The italic is clean, consistent and distinct, with even colour, but a little cold.
K2.small_why: The 13 px text is open, crisp and very comfortable to read.

K3.stone_why: The all-capital classical forms evoke engraved lettering, even though the overall effect is more ornamental than solid.
K3.carving_why: The curves and terminals are smooth and refined, with no visible chisel facets.
K3.calm_why: The swashed bold capitals and caps-only body text make the page busy and theatrical.
K3.personality_why: It is very distinctive, though the decorative flourishes push it toward fantasy rather than quiet stone.
K3.inscription_why: The regular capitals have good Roman proportions and dignity, but the bold weight turns into decorative swashes.
K3.oblique_why: The italic is a slanted small-caps texture with flourishes, so it barely reads as emphasis and is awkward at 13 px.
K3.small_why: The 13 px body set entirely in small capitals is tiring and hard to scan at phone size.

K4.stone_why: The polygonal, slightly irregular outlines look like letters cut into rock by hand.
K4.carving_why: SISIFO and the set numbers are made of crisp, flat facets on every curve, clearly chiselled rather than drawn.
K4.calm_why: The texture is grounded but slightly rough and uneven, and the bold weight barely differs from regular.
K4.personality_why: Its hand-cut, imperfect stone feel is unique and fits the Sisyphus theme closely.
K4.inscription_why: The capitals have classical proportions and serifs, with a rustic rather than formal-imperial cut.
K4.oblique_why: The italic is a lively calligraphic hand with an uneven, bouncy texture that is distinct but a little lumpy at 13 px.
K4.small_why: The 13 px roman is readable and open, though the faceted outlines soften slightly at small sizes.

K5.stone_why: The flared, glyphic serif with faceted curves reads like a carved monument inscription.
K5.carving_why: At display size the O, S, 6 and 5 show clean flat-cut facets and sharp flared terminals.
K5.calm_why: It is quiet and even, with presence, and only a slight nervousness in the faceted heavy numerals.
K5.personality_why: A memorable chiselled, classical voice that suits the app's grounded tone.
K5.inscription_why: The capitals have wide Roman proportions, flared strokes and real inscriptional dignity.
K5.oblique_why: The italic has a consistent slant and even colour, is clearly distinct, and reads well as emphasis.
K5.small_why: The 13 px lines are clear and comfortable, with slightly wide spacing but nothing clotting.

K6.stone_why: The heavy wedge-serif forms feel solid and engraved, though rather like Victorian print.
K6.carving_why: The serifs are sharp, cut wedges, but the bowls and curves are smooth ink rather than faceted.
K6.calm_why: The dark weight and very bold display lines feel heavy and somewhat loud.
K6.personality_why: The wedge serifs and the odd g give it a distinct, old-fashioned character.
K6.inscription_why: The capitals are heavy and closely spaced, closer to a display serif than to Roman inscriptional caps.
K6.oblique_why: A proper italic with a consistent slant, but the dark colour makes the notes lines heavy.
K6.small_why: The 13 px text is legible but dark and slightly dense.

K7.stone_why: An elegant, classical transitional serif that feels refined and bookish more than carved.
K7.carving_why: Its display sizes have smooth curves and bracketed serifs with no chiselled facets.
K7.calm_why: The rhythm is very even, with a quiet, composed presence.
K7.personality_why: It is handsome but conventional, a familiar editorial serif.
K7.inscription_why: The capitals have good classical proportions and dignity, if more typographic than inscribed.
K7.oblique_why: A true italic with an even slant and colour, clearly distinct and graceful at 13 px.
K7.small_why: The 13 px lines are sharp, open and very comfortable.

K8.stone_why: The flared sans nods to glyphic lettering but feels light and humanist rather than stone-cut.
K8.carving_why: The stroke flare is smooth and continuous, with no facets at display sizes.
K8.calm_why: It is calm, open and evenly paced, with no aggression.
K8.personality_why: A pleasant, Optima-like humanist sans that is somewhat familiar.
K8.inscription_why: The flared capitals echo inscriptional proportions and stroke modulation reasonably well.
K8.oblique_why: The italic is consistent and readable, clearly distinct though somewhat soft.
K8.small_why: The 13 px text is clean, open and very easy to read.

M1.stone_why: The 60 and 5 inputs are visibly faceted and carved, but the Bench press title is smooth.
M1.hierarchy_why: Title, chip, set table and big inputs are clearly distinct and orderly, with a large empty band mid-screen.

M2.stone_why: The This week title and the card values look smooth, with no carved display numbers on screen.
M2.hierarchy_why: Each card's label, bold value and grey detail read clearly in a calm, even stack.

M3.stone_why: The History title is a smooth serif, and there are no large numbers to carry the carved feel.
M3.hierarchy_why: The spaced date headings, session titles and tags separate cleanly into a quiet list.

M4.stone_why: The input numbers are faceted and carved, while the title remains smooth.
M4.hierarchy_why: Roles stay distinct; the rest-timer button adds one more element but the screen stays orderly.

M5.stone_why: The title also shows faint cut edges, matching the faceted 60 and 5 inputs.
M5.hierarchy_why: Title, chip, set table and inputs are distinct and calm, with the same empty mid-screen band.

M6.stone_why: The History title has slightly angular, cut outlines, but there are no big numbers to show carving.
M6.hierarchy_why: The date headings, titles and tags are clearly layered in a quiet list.

M7.stone_why: The inputs are carved, but the slightly smaller title is smooth.
M7.hierarchy_why: The tighter layout keeps the roles distinct, with the inputs lower and the table more compact.

M8.stone_why: Both the title and the input numbers show crisp cut facets.
M8.hierarchy_why: The compact layout reads clearly and calmly from title to table to inputs.

M9.stone_why: The This week title has slightly cut outlines, but the card values remain fairly smooth.
M9.hierarchy_why: Each card's label, value and detail are clearly ranked in an even, calm stack.

M10.stone_why: The title shows cut edges, and the 60 and 5 inputs are clearly faceted.
M10.hierarchy_why: The roles stay distinct and orderly, with the rest-timer button placed out of the way.
